title: wire.h struct mismatch vs uapi: unsigned int vs __u32 for fields that cross ABI boundary
description: crypto2dev_wire.h defines struct fields using 'unsigned int' and 'int'. The actual kernel uapi header (crypto2dev_ioctl.h) defines the same fields as __u32 and __s32 (explicitly sized Linux kernel types). On LP64 Linux, 'unsigned int' is 32 bits and 'int' is 32 bits — same as __u32/__s32 — so this happens to be correct today. But: if this code is ever built for a platform where 'unsigned int' is 16 bits (C89 guarantees only 'at least 16 bits'), the struct sizes would differ from the kernel's, the compile-time wc_static_assert2 guards would fire, but only at build time on that platform. More concretely, the wire.h structs use 'char' for algo/provider fields vs the uapi header's explicit 'char'. That part is fine. The concern is future-proofing: wire.h should use exact-width types (uint32_t/int32_t from stdint.h or __u32/__s32 with appropriate guards) not 'unsigned int'. The assert guards exist precisely because of this but they catch it only at build time, not enforce it lexically.
